report.clinical_summary: Patient with CLL experiencing significant fatigue and night sweats that impact daily life, work, family, and emotional well-being. New medication causing headaches and side effects. Patient engages in self-care practices but recognizes limits. Believes CLL is slow-moving and may not need treatment, but still feels uncertain and worried about progression. Values treatment for monitoring and reassurance, but has concerns about long-term effects and whether it's worth it. Sees medicines as generally helpful but cautious about side effects and interactions. Believes doctors can be quick to reach for medication.

evidence.quote: I've found that focusing on some key self-care practices has been really helpful in managing my condition. Those include trying to get regular exercise (even if just a short walk most days), getting enough sleep, eating reasonably well and staying engaged with activities I enjoy.

But at the same time, it can feel like there's only so much I can control. There are limits to how much lifestyle changes or self-care practices can influence my situation — especially when you factor in the underlying impact of this disease on my body.

That said, I do think that maintaining a positive mindset and focusing on what I can do rather than what I can't does make a difference — even if it's just small differences. It helps me feel more empowered, less overwhelmed by everything happening at once.
